CubeDistance_mm.blurb: How far (mm) beside a light-cube face the planner-test stand-off pose is placed. Default 25; console range 0–100. Only used by the DevPlannerTest behavior: for each cube face it aims at, it builds a goal pose offset by this distance along the face’s local −Y (and half cube height down), then DriveToPose-loops cube ↔ far pose.
CubeDistance_mm.detail: BehaviorPlannerTest (JSON DevPlannerTest) finds located light cubes, picks approach poses from vertical face markers (or top when the cube is on its side), and constructs each goal as Point3f{0, −CubeDistance_mm, −halfHeight} relative to that marker, rotated π/2 about Z. Does nothing in normal freeplay — only when that dev behavior is activated. Sibling Distance_mm (same category) is the far-away drive distance after reaching the cube.
CubeDistance_mm.statusNote: Live only while BehaviorPlannerTest / DevPlannerTest is activated; freeplay ignores it.

CubeTriggerIdx.blurb: Index into the DevViewCubeBackpackLights behavior’s JSON list of cube light animation triggers. Change the number to play the next cube-light pattern on a connected light cube. Default 0. Out-of-range values clamp to the last entry in the list.
CubeTriggerIdx.detail: Category DevViewLights. On each BehaviorUpdate while DevViewCubeBackpackLights is active, if this index differs from the last applied value the behavior finds a connected light cube and calls PlayLightAnimByTrigger / StopAndPlayLightAnim for cubeTriggers[validIdx] from the behavior JSON. Independent sibling BackpackTriggerIdx drives backpack LEDs the same way. Without that dev behavior running and without a connected cube, changing this does nothing.
CubeTriggerIdx.howTo: 1) Activate behavior DevViewCubeBackpackLights. 2) Connect a light cube. 3) Set CubeTriggerIdx to step through cubeTriggers in the behavior JSON.

paths.notes: cubeTriggers array supplies the animation trigger names this index selects.

CubeTriggerIdx.statusNote: Only applied while DevViewCubeBackpackLights is activated and a connected light cube is found.

DebugPossibleBlockInteraction.blurb: When true, every engine visualization tick logs one debug line per located light cube: pose state, moving/flat/carried flags, relative Z, up-axis, and whether docking thinks the robot can stack on / pick up the cube (including from ground). Off by default. Visualization-only logging — does not change interaction rules.
DebugPossibleBlockInteraction.detail: Registered under category Robot. Read inside Robot::Update’s ENABLE_DRAWING block (ENABLE_DRAWING = ANKI_DEV_CHEATS). Uses BlockWorldFilter::IsLightCubeFilter and DockingComponent CanStackOnTopOfObject / CanPickUpObject / CanPickUpObjectFromGround. Log channel key Robot.ObjectInteractionState. Can flood logs if many cubes are tracked every 60 ms tick.
DebugPossibleBlockInteraction.statusNote: Use path is compiled only when ANKI_DEV_CHEATS (ENABLE_DRAWING). On builds without that, the var may still appear but the if-body is gone.

DriveToAndPickupBlockOneAction.blurb: Docking-test mode switch (default true). When the DockingTestSimple behavior is about to pick up a block and JustPickup is false: true runs a single combined DriveToPickupObjectAction (or align+lift compound if AlignInsteadOfPickup); false splits drive-to-object and pickup into two sequential states.
DriveToAndPickupBlockOneAction.detail: Category DockingTest. Only consulted in BehaviorDockingTestSimple’s pickup branch after JustPickup is checked. Combined path uses DriveToPickupObjectAction with TestDockingMethod, or DriveToAlignWithObjectAction(LIFT_PLATE)+MoveLiftToHeight(CARRY) when AlignInsteadOfPickup. Split path uses DriveToObjectAction then PickupObjectAction. Does not affect product freeplay pickup — only the docking stress-test behavior.
DriveToAndPickupBlockOneAction.statusNote: Live only while DockingTestSimple is running; ignored in freeplay.

ExpectedCubePoseAngleThresh_rad.blurb: Factory playpen only: max allowed rotation difference (radians) between the observed paperclip light cube (LIGHTCUBE1) and the expected fixture pose when PlaypenPickupCube checks placement. Default DEG_TO_RAD(10) ≈ 0.175 rad. Larger = looser angle pass.
ExpectedCubePoseAngleThresh_rad.detail: PlaypenConfig value wrapped under category Playpen. Passed to Pose3d::IsSameAs_WithAmbiguity with upright-only rotation ambiguities and ExpectedCubePoseDistThresh_mm. Failures set FactoryTestResultCode::CUBE_NOT_WHERE_EXPECTED. Freeplay never reads this.

ExpectedCubePoseDistThresh_mm.blurb: Factory playpen only: max allowed XY translation error (mm) between observed LIGHTCUBE1 pose and the expected fixture pose during PlaypenPickupCube. Default 30 mm. Failures report CUBE_NOT_WHERE_EXPECTED.
ExpectedCubePoseDistThresh_mm.detail: Paired with ExpectedCubePoseAngleThresh_rad in IsSameAs_WithAmbiguity (upright rotation ambiguities only). Expected position comes from ExpectedCubePoseX/Y (defaults 420, 0 mm in world origin frame) with Z fixed at 22 mm in the behavior’s static expected pose. Height is checked separately via ExpectedCubePoseHeightThresh_mm.

ExpectedCubePoseHeightThresh_mm.blurb: Factory playpen only: max allowed |cube_center_z − half_cube_height| (mm) when PlaypenPickupCube validates that the cube is sitting at a sane height. Default 10 mm. Too high → CUBE_HEIGHT_TOO_HIGH; too low → CUBE_HEIGHT_TOO_LOW (compared against expected pose Z = 22 mm).
ExpectedCubePoseHeightThresh_mm.detail: Separate from the XY/angle IsSameAs check. Uses observed translation.z() minus 0.5×object size.z() as the residual; if |residual| exceeds this threshold, classifies high vs low using expected pose Z. Does not affect freeplay object filtering.

ExpectedCubePoseX_mm.blurb: Factory playpen only: expected world-X (mm) of the paperclip light cube relative to the playpen starting / world origin when PlaypenPickupCube verifies placement. Default 420 mm. Documents the fixture layout; see statusNote about console liveness.
ExpectedCubePoseX_mm.detail: Declared in PlaypenConfig and WRAP_EXTERN_CONSOLE_VAR-registered under Playpen. behaviorPlaypenPickupCube builds a file-static const Pose3d once from X, Y, and Z=22 at load time, then copies it when the check runs. Observed LIGHTCUBE1 must match that pose within Dist/Angle thresh (with upright ambiguities) or the test fails CUBE_NOT_WHERE_EXPECTED. Changing this console value after process start does not rebuild that static Pose3d.
ExpectedCubePoseX_mm.statusNote: Default 420 is used to initialize a file-static const expected pose at load. Runtime console sets do not re-read X into that pose. Only meaningful in PlaypenPickupCube.

ExpectedCubePoseY_mm.blurb: Factory playpen only: expected world-Y (mm) of the paperclip light cube for PlaypenPickupCube’s placement check. Default 0 (on the playpen centerline). Same static-pose caveat as ExpectedCubePoseX_mm.
ExpectedCubePoseY_mm.detail: Paired with ExpectedCubePoseX_mm when building the static expected Pose3d (Z fixed 22). Observed cube must be within Dist/Angle thresholds of that pose. Console registration under Playpen; freeplay never uses it.
ExpectedCubePoseY_mm.statusNote: Default 0 baked into file-static const expected pose at load; runtime console changes do not rebuild it. PlaypenPickupCube only.

IReallyReallyWantToBreakCubeSpinner.blurb: When true, Vector still plays the cube-spinner “tap/lock” animation but does not call the game’s LockNow() — so the software game never registers Vector’s tap as locking the current light. Default false. Product Cube Spinner (VectorPlaysCubeSpinner) normally fakes a successful lock because real lift taps are unreliable.
IReallyReallyWantToBreakCubeSpinner.detail: Category CubeSpinner. Authors’ comment: spinner depends on faking the lock due to gear/lift, cube sensitivity, anim pressure variants, and light lag; vision does not confirm the light. TapIfAppropriate still schedules PlayAnimationAction for the lock anim, then skips cubeSpinnerGame->LockNow() if this flag is true — desyncing animation from game state (missed locks, stuck rounds, hard-to-repro bugs). Leave false unless deliberately stress-testing failure modes.
IReallyReallyWantToBreakCubeSpinner.statusNote: Live in freeplay Cube Spinner. Intentionally breaks game/animation coupling; do not enable casually.
